title: Why Short Breaks Can Improve Concentration
instructions: Read the passage and choose the best answer according to the text.

paragraphs: Many students believe that successful studying means sitting at a desk for several hours without stopping. They may feel guilty when they stand up, look out of the window, or make a drink. However, attention is not a machine that can work at the same level all day. Researchers who study learning often point out that planned short breaks can protect concentration instead of damaging it. The important distinction is between a controlled break and an unplanned distraction.

When people work on one task for a long time, their attention gradually becomes weaker. They may continue reading, but they begin to notice fewer details and remember less. A short change of activity can interrupt this decline. Walking across the room, stretching, or drinking water gives the mind a clear signal that one work period has ended. When students return, they can approach the material with fresher attention. The break does not need to be long; five minutes may be enough after a focused period of study.

Not every break has the same effect. Opening social media for a minute can easily become twenty minutes because the platforms are designed to keep users interested. Emotional messages and rapidly changing videos also fill the mind with new information. As a result, students may find it difficult to return to a quiet textbook. Breaks that involve light movement, fresh air, or a simple physical task are usually easier to control. They rest the mind without creating a second demanding activity.

Planning matters as much as the break itself. Some students use a timer and decide in advance what they will complete before it rings. This turns a large and unclear task into a smaller target. For example, instead of saying, 'I will study biology all evening,' a student can decide to read six pages and write five review questions. The following break then becomes part of the plan rather than an escape from difficult work. After the break, the student chooses the next small target.

Short breaks are not a magical solution for every learning problem. A student who sleeps very little or studies in a noisy room may still struggle to focus. In addition, difficult topics sometimes require a longer period of thought before taking a break. The useful principle is flexibility: notice when attention is falling, choose a break that is easy to end, and return with a specific next action. In this way, rest supports discipline instead of replacing it.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.A: To argue that all study periods should have the same length
options.B: To explain how planned breaks may support effective studying
options.C: To show why students should avoid difficult subjects
options.D: To compare university libraries with home study

questions.rationale: The passage explains when and how short, controlled breaks can protect concentration.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, what may happen during a very long work period?

options.A: Students read faster and remember more
options.B: Attention weakens even if the person continues reading
options.D: The material becomes easier by itself

questions.rationale: The paragraph states that people may keep reading while noticing and remembering less.

questions.stem: Why can social media be an ineffective break?

options.A: It usually requires students to leave the room
options.B: It prevents students from using a timer
options.C: It can be difficult to stop and adds more information

questions.rationale: The text says platforms hold attention and fill the mind with new information.

questions.stem: The word 'decline' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to _____.
questions.rationale: Decline refers to attention becoming gradually weaker.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about setting small targets?

options.A: It can make a large task feel more manageable
options.B: It removes the need to understand the material
options.C: It is useful only for biology students

questions.rationale: Specific small targets turn a large unclear task into manageable work periods.

questions.stem: Which statement would the writer most likely agree with?

options.A: A break is useful no matter how it is spent
options.B: Students should stop as soon as a topic becomes difficult
options.C: Good breaks are planned, limited, and followed by a clear action
options.D: Concentration problems are always caused by phones

questions.rationale: The conclusion recommends controlled breaks and a specific action for returning to work.
